title: FinOps for Manufacturing IT: Controlling Cloud Cost for Industrial Workloads
description:
Factories running the same machines often pay more to collect, process and keep the data those machines produce each shift. This episode is for manufacturing IT, platform engineers and finance teams who need to control Azure and Microsoft Fabric costs without losing the evidence behind downtime and quality investigations. It walks through baselines, telemetry, retention, capacity, commitments and fair allocation across plants.
In this episode
00:00 – Why factory cloud costs grow04:08 – FinOps ownership in manufacturing07:32 – Building a shared cost baseline14:05 – Telemetry, gateways and delivery32:06 – Retention and storage tiers44:03 – Fabric capacity and shared compute56:38 – Commitments and reservations70:33 – Allocation, showback and chargeback
Key takeaways
In manufacturing, cloud spend follows data handling decisions, so every cost change needs a named owner who understands the evidence and service level the plant depends on.A shared cost baseline, deliberate retention and storage-tier choices, and tested Fabric capacity sizing prevent savings that silently remove fault or quality evidence.Commitments, allocation rules and showback before chargeback only work when unused commitment, shared fixed costs and funding authority are made explicit.
